items.title: Adopt the four-field token model (cache tokens) in usage shape + JSON example
items.context: In the 'JSON Ledger Record Shape' section and its example, replace inputTokens/outputTokens/totalTokens with the full Anthropic shape: inputTokens (uncached remainder), outputTokens, cacheCreationInputTokens, cacheReadInputTokens — as first-class fields (or mandate them as required billableUnits[] entries). Add a sentence stating input_tokens is the uncached remainder, not total. Reference that CMA's span.model_request_end.model_usage already uses these four fields.

happy.desc: grep the JSON example block -> contains cacheCreationInputTokens AND cacheReadInputTokens AND inputTokens AND outputTokens as four distinct fields; WHY: the example is the de-facto spec, must show all four cache-aware token fields
prose states that inputTokens (or input_tokens) is the uncached remainder, not the total input -> grep for uncached remainder; WHY: prevents implementer misreading inputTokens as gross input
doc references CMA span.model_request_end.model_usage (or Managed Agents model_usage) as prior art -> grep for model_usage or model_request_end; WHY: establishes provenance for the four-field shape

Required record constraints section mentions all four token fields as required (or specifies when-required semantics) -> grep constraints section for cacheCreation and cacheRead; WHY: folds in product-reviewer advisory about constraints clarity

edge.desc: JSON example does NOT contain a totalTokens field (CHK-002 removes it but CHK-001 example should already omit or CHK-002 will) -> grep for totalTokens inside JSON block -> expect absent OR expect CHK-002 removes it; WHY: catch inconsistency if CHK-001 adds four fields but leaves stale totalTokens

billableUnits array in the example, if still present, includes cache-type entries (cache_creation, cache_read) or the example omits billableUnits entirely -> grep billableUnits; WHY: catch stale billableUnits that only lists input/output without cache

adversarial.desc: search entire doc for the string totalTokens -> must appear ONLY in derived/summary context (CHK-002), never as a stored field in the record shape or example; WHY: adversarial check that old two-field model is fully purged from record-level prose
verify no source-code files (.ts, .js, .json schema files) are modified in the git diff for this story -> git diff --name-only vs main; WHY: scope creep guard -- this is doc-only

items.title: Remove derived totalTokens as a stored field; define the identity in the summary layer
items.context: Delete totalTokens from the append record (derived fields drift and are ambiguous once cache tokens exist). State the identity total_processed = inputTokens + outputTokens + cacheCreationInputTokens + cacheReadInputTokens, and require totals to be computed in the ledger summary layer, not stored per-record.

happy.desc: grep entire JSON example block for totalTokens -> absent; WHY: totalTokens is a derived field and must not be stored per-record

doc contains the identity formula total_processed = inputTokens + outputTokens + cacheCreationInputTokens + cacheReadInputTokens (or equivalent) -> grep for the identity; WHY: the summary layer must define how totals are computed
prose explicitly states totals are computed in the summary layer, not stored per-record -> grep for summary layer or summary-derived; WHY: prevents implementers from re-adding totalTokens

edge.desc: grep Required record constraints for totalTokens -> absent; WHY: catch constraints section still listing totalTokens as required even after example removal
grep billableUnits entries for a total-type entry -> absent; WHY: catch totalTokens smuggled back via billableUnits

adversarial.desc: count all occurrences of totalTokens in the entire doc -> each occurrence must be in a context that says derived/summary/not-stored; WHY: adversarial full-text scan to catch any stale reference that still treats totalTokens as a stored field
grep Validation/Smoke Plan for totalTokens -> must reference its removal or absence, not assert its presence; WHY: catch stale validation assertion that still tests for stored totalTokens

items.title: Estimate accuracy: prefer provider count_tokens; rank estimator confidence; bind to model ID
items.context: In 'Usage Source Semantics' and the Estimate path, require prompt-size-estimate to prefer the provider's count_tokens endpoint (model-version-specific — counts differ across model versions), falling back to local tokenizer then bytes/chars only when offline. Record estimator confidence high|medium|low accordingly and require the estimate to be tied to the exact provider.model.

happy.desc: doc mentions count_tokens as the preferred estimation method (provider endpoint) -> grep for count_tokens; WHY: ensures estimate path prefers provider tokenizer over local heuristics
doc specifies estimator confidence ranking high|medium|low -> grep for confidence and high|medium|low; WHY: ensures estimate records carry a confidence discriminator

doc requires estimate to be bound to exact provider.model (model-version-specific) -> grep for model-version or provider.model in estimate context; WHY: counts differ across model versions, binding prevents stale estimates

edge.desc: fallback chain is explicitly ordered: count_tokens > local tokenizer > bytes/chars -> grep for fallback or ordered preference; WHY: catch missing fallback order that would leave implementers guessing

estimator.name and estimator.version still required in constraints alongside new confidence field -> grep constraints for estimator; WHY: catch regression where adding confidence drops existing estimator fields

adversarial.desc: grep entire doc for bytes-per-char or bytes heuristic as a PRIMARY estimator (not fallback) -> must only appear as lowest-confidence fallback; WHY: adversarial check that cheap heuristics are not accidentally promoted to preferred
grep JSON example for estimator block -> if present, must include confidence field; WHY: catch example updated with estimator but missing the new confidence field, creating prose-example mismatch

items.title: Call-time story/phase attribution rules
items.context: Specify that storyId/phase are captured from the active lease/session context at preflight (call time). Non-story calls (global validate, daemon) record storyId=null and are NOT dropped. Subagent/nested calls propagate the parent storyId plus a subagent/thread id. Add a role/agentType field (implementer|reviewer|main|...) so per-story breakdowns by role are possible.

happy.desc: doc specifies storyId=null for non-story calls (global validate, daemon) and explicitly states they are NOT dropped -> grep for storyId and null; WHY: non-story usage must still be recorded
doc describes subagent/nested call propagation of parent storyId plus subagent/thread id -> grep for subagent or nested or propagat; WHY: ensures nested calls are traceable to parent story
doc adds role or agentType field (implementer|reviewer|main or similar) -> grep for role or agentType; WHY: enables per-story breakdown by role
doc specifies storyId/phase captured at preflight (call time) from active lease/session context -> grep for preflight or call time in attribution context; WHY: prevents post-hoc attribution errors

edge.desc: JSON example block includes storyId field (already present) and now also includes role/agentType field -> grep JSON example for agentType or role; WHY: catch prose-updated-but-example-not inconsistency
subagent propagation specifies a subagentId or threadId field in the record -> grep for subagentId or threadId; WHY: without an id field, subagent propagation is unimplementable

adversarial.desc: grep for any statement that drops or filters out storyId=null records -> must be absent; WHY: adversarial check that null-story records are not silently excluded from summaries
grep for storyId in Validation/Smoke Plan -> must assert null-storyId recording and subagent propagation; WHY: catch stale Validation section that does not test the new attribution rules

items.title: Completeness guarantee: single writer choke-point + reconciliation
items.context: Add a section requiring all provider dispatch to flow through a single ledger-writing choke-point, plus a periodic reconciliation check (count of provider dispatch events vs count of ledger final records per ledgerCallId+attemptId) that surfaces gaps. Accuracy = completeness, not just per-record correctness; a bypassed writer silently under-counts.

happy.desc: doc contains a section (or subsection) about single writer choke-point requiring all provider dispatch to flow through one ledger-writing path -> grep for choke-point or single writer; WHY: ensures completeness by construction

doc contains a reconciliation section/paragraph describing periodic check of dispatch events vs ledger records -> grep for reconciliation or reconcil; WHY: catch completeness gaps where dispatch bypasses the writer

edge.desc: reconciliation references ledgerCallId+attemptId as the correlation key -> grep reconciliation context for ledgerCallId; WHY: reconciliation without the right key is unimplementable
doc addresses the failure mode of a bypassed writer (silent under-count) -> grep for bypass or under-count or silent; WHY: motivates why the choke-point exists

adversarial.desc: grep Implementation Touchpoints for any new implementation slice that could bypass the choke-point (e.g., a second writer path) -> must not introduce contradictory multi-writer guidance; WHY: adversarial check for internal doc contradiction
grep Validation/Smoke Plan for reconciliation or completeness assertion -> must be present; WHY: catch stale Validation that omits completeness testing

items.title: Streaming and failure usage capture
items.context: Clarify that for streaming responses, final usage must be read from the terminal stream event (message_delta / final message), not assumed from a non-streaming shape; and a call that errors/times out mid-stream still records the partial output usage it consumed. usage.source=unavailable only when truly no count exists.

happy.desc: doc specifies streaming usage must be read from the terminal stream event (message_delta or final message) -> grep for terminal stream event or message_delta; WHY: streaming responses require reading usage from the last event, not assuming non-streaming shape
doc specifies partial output usage on error/timeout mid-stream must still be recorded -> grep for partial or error or timeout in streaming context; WHY: errored calls still consume budget
doc clarifies usage.source=unavailable only when truly no count exists -> grep for unavailable and truly or no reliable; WHY: prevents lazy unavailable marking when partial counts are available

edge.desc: existing rule about failed requests writing ledger entries (line 81 area) is consistent with new streaming/failure guidance -> grep for failed request in both existing and new sections; WHY: catch contradiction between existing failure rule and new streaming failure rule

if streaming section references provider-reported source, it specifies that partial counts from a terminal event still qualify as provider-reported -> grep for provider-reported near streaming; WHY: partial real counts should not be downgraded to estimate

adversarial.desc: grep entire doc for any statement that sets unavailable usage to zero or treats missing as zero-cost -> must be absent or explicitly prohibited; WHY: adversarial check for the most dangerous accounting error
grep Validation/Smoke Plan for streaming or partial or failure usage assertion -> must be present; WHY: catch stale Validation that omits streaming/failure test

items.title: Multi-provider: raw fidelity + normalized canonical view
items.context: Resolve the tension between 'preserve provider-specific units' and 'cross-source summaries' by requiring BOTH: keep the raw provider units/payload digest AND a normalized canonical {input, output, cacheCreation, cacheRead} view, with explicit mapping rules for how each provider's cache/cached-token fields map to the canonical cache fields.

happy.desc: doc requires BOTH raw provider units AND a normalized canonical view {input, output, cacheCreation, cacheRead} -> grep for canonical or normalized and raw or provider-specific; WHY: resolves the tension between fidelity and cross-source summaries

doc includes explicit mapping rules for how each providers cache/cached-token fields map to the canonical cache fields -> grep for mapping or map; WHY: without mapping rules, normalization is unimplementable

edge.desc: canonical view uses {input, output, cacheCreation, cacheRead} (four fields matching CHK-001) not a different set -> grep for canonical field names; WHY: catch inconsistency between CHK-001 four-field model and CHK-007 canonical names

provider adapter extraction touchpoint (existing section 2) is consistent with new dual-view requirement -> grep Implementation Touchpoints section 2 for canonical or raw; WHY: catch contradiction between existing touchpoint and new requirement

adversarial.desc: grep for any statement that discards raw provider units in favor of only the canonical view -> must be absent; WHY: adversarial check that raw fidelity is not lost despite normalization

JSON example includes both raw provider units (e.g., billableUnits or provider-specific block) and canonical fields -> grep example for both; WHY: catch prose-updated-but-example-not showing only one view

items.title: Cost derivability: price/pricingRef snapshot
items.context: Add that cost is derived only in a layer that pins model+date to a price table (per-model $/MTok + cache multipliers, which change over time). Record a pricingVersion/pricingRef (not a hardcoded price) on the record or specify the snapshot mechanism; do not bake absolute prices into the append-only record beyond a reference.

happy.desc: doc adds pricingRef or pricingVersion field for cost derivation -> grep for pricingRef or pricingVersion; WHY: cost must be derived from a pinned price table, not hardcoded

doc specifies snapshot mechanism or price table (per-model per-MTok + cache multipliers, which change over time) -> grep for snapshot or price table or multiplier; WHY: prices change, so records must reference a versioned table
doc explicitly prohibits absolute prices baked into append-only records -> grep for absolute price or hardcoded or baked; WHY: prevents per-record cost fields that become stale when prices change

edge.desc: JSON example record does NOT contain a cost or price field with a dollar amount -> grep JSON example for cost or price with numeric values; WHY: catch example contradicting the no-absolute-prices rule

doc addresses cache multipliers (cache reads cost less, cache writes cost more than base input) in pricing context -> grep for cache and multiplier or cost; WHY: cache tokens have different per-token costs, pricing must handle this

adversarial.desc: grep entire doc for any hardcoded dollar amount -> must be absent from record-level prose; WHY: adversarial check for accidentally baked-in prices
grep Acceptance Criteria for pricing or pricingRef -> must be mentioned; WHY: catch stale Acceptance Criteria that omits the pricing constraint

items.title: Update Validation/Smoke Plan, Acceptance Criteria, and Rollout to cover the new fields
items.context: Extend the Validation/Smoke Plan, Acceptance Criteria, and Rollout Phases sections so they assert: four-field cache-token recording, no stored totalTokens, estimator confidence + count_tokens preference, call-time attribution incl. null/subagent, completeness reconciliation, streaming/failure usage, canonical normalization, and pricingRef. Keep cross-references consistent throughout the doc.
